correctness.rationale: The ratio e-value is strictly increasing from zero to \(n+1\), so solving \(1-\lambda+\lambda e(v)<h\) gives exactly the all-positive or finite-interval dichotomy and the displayed endpoint. Differentiation proves strict endpoint decrease on the finite branch. Since the infimum over positive candidate scores of post-batch wealth is \(W(1-\lambda)\), the reserve condition is exactly \(\lambda\le1-R/W\), and choosing the largest feasible fraction minimizes the current set. Fresh independent rational checks reproduced the endpoint classification and reserve inequality over randomized parameter instances.
